skill.name: content-strategy
skill.description: Helps teams plan content strategy, choose content pillars, map topic clusters, prioritize ideas, and connect searchable or shareable content to business goals.
skill.summary: Plan content pillars, topic clusters, and prioritized editorial roadmaps.
skill.author: coreyhaines31

content.value_statement: Teams often publish scattered content without clear priorities or buyer-stage coverage. This skill turns research, keywords, and customer insight into focused pillars, clusters, and topic roadmaps.
actual_capabilities: Checks for product marketing context before planning when available.
Separates searchable content from shareable content and explains when to use each.
Builds content pillars, topic clusters, and hub-and-spoke structures.
Maps keyword ideas to awareness, consideration, decision, and implementation stages.
Prioritizes ideas with customer impact, market fit, search potential, and resource effort.
Suggests research sources, including keyword data, calls, surveys, forums, and competitors.
limitations: It does not write complete articles or landing pages.
It needs audience, product, keyword, or customer context for precise recommendations.
It does not replace a technical SEO audit or analytics implementation review.
Forum and competitor research depends on available browsing tools and source quality.

use_cases.title: Launch a Content Program
use_cases.description: Create initial pillars, buyer-stage topics, and a publishing cadence for a new B2B content program.

use_cases.title: Restructure an Existing Blog
use_cases.description: Organize scattered posts into clusters, find gaps, and decide what to update, merge, or retire.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Limited Capacity
use_cases.description: Rank a long list of ideas by customer impact, product fit, search potential, and required effort.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Strategy
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new content program.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me create a content strategy for my business. Ask for missing context, then propose pillars, topic clusters, and first priorities.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Buyer-Stage Topics
prompt_templates.scenario: Map content ideas to the buyer journey.
prompt_templates.prompt: Build a content plan for these customers and product goals. Group topics by awareness, consideration, decision, and implementation stages.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Content Direction
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve a blog with many existing posts.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my current content themes and recommend a clearer strategy. Identify pillars, cluster gaps, updates, consolidations, and next topics.

prompt_templates.title: Prioritize a Roadmap
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning with limited team capacity.
prompt_templates.prompt: Score these content ideas using customer impact, content-market fit, search potential, and resource requirements. Recommend a practical roadmap.

output_examples.input: A B2B SaaS team needs a first content strategy for finance leaders.
output_examples.output: The skill returns core pillars, buyer-stage topic ideas, target keywords, and a publishing cadence tied to finance team pain points.

output_examples.input: A company has 200 blog posts with flat traffic and unclear themes.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends cluster categories, hub pages, posts to refresh, posts to consolidate, and missing topics to build topical authority.

output_examples.input: A small team has 50 article ideas and only one writer.
output_examples.output: The skill ranks ideas by impact and effort, then creates a focused short-term roadmap for the available writing capacity.

best_practices: Provide customer research, sales objections, keyword data, and existing content performance when available.
Use the prioritization framework before building an editorial calendar.
Review clusters regularly so new posts support existing authority instead of creating isolated topics.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to write complete articles instead of planning strategy.
Do not build only top-of-funnel content without consideration and decision-stage coverage.
Do not treat competitor topics as automatic priorities without customer and product fit.

faq.question: What does this skill help plan?
faq.answer: It plans content pillars, topic clusters, buyer-stage topics, prioritization, and content roadmap structure.

faq.question: Can it write the final blog post?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on strategy and recommends using a copywriting skill for full drafts.

faq.question: Does it support SEO planning?
faq.answer: Yes. It maps keywords, search intent, buyer stages, and hub-and-spoke structures for content planning.

faq.question: What inputs improve results?
faq.answer: Useful inputs include customer calls, support themes, keyword exports, competitor names, product positioning, and current content performance.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Content marketers, founders, growth teams, and product marketers can use it to plan higher-value content.

faq.question: Does it work for existing content libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. It can organize existing posts into clusters and suggest updates, consolidations, or new supporting topics.
